text:
Minnesota is the favorite tonight, with the model projecting 3.35 expected goals for the Wild against 2.78 for Columbus. Part of that is rest: the Blue Jackets are on the second night of a back-to-back after a 1-0 overtime win over the Rangers, while the Wild have had two days off. Minnesota generates 3.47 expected goals per 60 and allows 2.96. Columbus sits at 3.01 for and 3.23 against. At five on five the two are nearly even, with CBJ at 51% of the expected goals and MIN at 50%. The Wild do have the better special teams numbers, and Columbus takes 4.2 penalties a game, which keeps giving the other side power plays. Minnesota will be without Jared Spurgeon (upper body).

The goalie matchup also favors the home side. Projected starter Jesper Wallstedt is at +6.0 goals saved above expected this season (.920) after +5.8 last year, and he has been strong against hard shots lately. Columbus projects to start Cam Talbot, who is at -2.3 this season (.822) after -13.7 last year over 34 games.

Recent form leans Minnesota too. The Wild are 3-2-0 in their last five with 55% of the expected goals, while Columbus is 2-3-0 with 48%. Kirill Kaprizov is the player to watch, at 49% to score and 76% to record a point, and Matt Boldy sits at 46% to score. For Columbus, Kent Johnson has 5 points in his last six games, though much of that is finishing luck, and he is 20% to score tonight.
